# GBM Analysis

```{r Load_Files}

folder <- "C:/Users/lucas/OneDrive/ALL PC STUFF/Desktop/GBM Data"

files <- list.files(
  path = folder,
  pattern = "\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)


data_list <- lapply(files, read.csv)


names(data_list) <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(files))

# Display available stock tickers
names(data_list)


View(data_list[[1]])
```

Select Stock from Ticker, Start and End Date, extract Price data used with checks for validity of data

```{r choose-initial-stock}

# Choose initial stock
Chosen_Stock <- "AAF"

# Choose start and end dates
start_date <- as.Date("2020-01-01")
end_date   <- as.Date("2022-12-31")

# Various tests for validity of date ranges, fields, formats and completeness
if (is.na(start_date) || is.na(end_date) || start_date > end_date) {
  stop("Invalid date range: check that start_date is before or equal to end_date.")
}

if (!Chosen_Stock %in% names(data_list)) {
  stop(paste0(
    "Stock '", Chosen_Stock,
    "' was not found in data_list. Check the ticker name."
  ))
}

# Load selected stock
stock <- data_list[[Chosen_Stock]]

if (!"close" %in% names(stock)) {
  stop(paste0(
    "Stock '", Chosen_Stock,
    "' does not contain a 'close' column."
  ))
}

if (!"date" %in% names(stock)) {
  stop(paste0(
    "Stock '", Chosen_Stock,
    "' does not contain a 'date' column. Check the actual column name."
  ))
}

# Convert dates and extract closing prices
all_dates <- as.Date(stock$date, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
all_prices <- stock$close

if (all(is.na(all_dates))) {
  stop("Date conversion failed. Check the date format in stock$date.")
}

# Select valid data within the requested date range
selected <- !is.na(all_dates) &
  all_dates >= start_date &
  all_dates <= end_date &
  is.finite(all_prices) &
  all_prices > 0
# All Prices > 0 is a constraint of the model 

# Stop if no valid prices exist in the selected period
if (!any(selected)) {
  stop(paste0(
    "No valid closing-price data for ", Chosen_Stock,
    " between ", format(start_date, "%Y-%m-%d"),
    " and ", format(end_date, "%Y-%m-%d"),
    ". Check the date range and date format."
  ))
}

# Keep only selected dates and prices
dates <- all_dates[selected]
prices <- all_prices[selected]

# Sort observations chronologically
ordering <- order(dates)
dates <- dates[ordering]
prices <- prices[ordering]

# Check sufficient data for returns and simulation
if (length(prices) < 2) {
  stop("Fewer than two valid prices are available. At least two are required.")
}

# Report successful selection
cat("Stock:", Chosen_Stock, "\n")
cat("Start date available:", format(min(dates), "%Y-%m-%d"), "\n")
cat("End date available:", format(max(dates), "%Y-%m-%d"), "\n")
cat("Number of prices:", length(prices), "\n")

```

Daily Log Returns over a yearly time period

```{r time-period}
log_returns <- diff(log(prices))

n <- length(log_returns)
trading_days <- 252
# 252 Business Days py
T <- n / trading_days

time <- seq(0, T, length.out = n + 1)

cat("Number of daily returns:", n, "\n")
cat("Approximate time period (years):", round(T, 2), "\n")
```

GBM Model Equation:

$$
S_t = S_0 \exp\left(\left(\mu - \frac{\sigma^2}{2}\right)t + \sigma W_t\right)
$$

Estimate Annual Drift and Velocity

```{r estimate-parameters}
sigma_hat <- sd(log_returns) * sqrt(trading_days)

mu_hat <- mean(log_returns) * trading_days +
  0.5 * sigma_hat^2

cat("Annualised drift:", round(mu_hat, 4), "\n")
cat("Annualised volatility:", round(sigma_hat, 4), "\n")
```

Simulate GBM Path

```{r simulate-gbm}
#generated fixed path, so can be compared between stocks
set.seed(123)

#generate n random numbers from normal distribution with parameters below
dW <- rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(1 / trading_days))
#Cumulative Sum to construct Brownian Path
W <- c(0, cumsum(dW))

#Applies GBM to every time point
simulated_prices <- prices[1] *
  exp((mu_hat - 0.5 * sigma_hat^2) * time +
        sigma_hat * W)
```

Historical Prices against simulated prices

```{r compare prices}
plot(dates, prices, type = "l",
     xlab = "Date", ylab = "Share price",
     main = paste(Chosen_Stock, ": Historical Prices vs GBM"))

lines(dates, simulated_prices, col = "red", lty = 2)
```

```{r compare-prices 2}

# Plot historical share prices
plot(
  dates, prices,
  type = "l",
  xlab = "Date",
  ylab = "Share price",
  main = paste(Chosen_Stock, ": Historical Prices vs GBM"),
  xaxt = "n"
)

# Add GBM prices
lines(dates, simulated_prices, col = "red", lty = 2)

# Add date labels
date_ticks <- pretty(dates, n = 6)
axis.Date(1, at = date_ticks, format = "%Y-%m")

# Add key
legend(
  "topleft",
  legend = c("Historical prices", "GBM simulation"),
  col = c("black", "red"),
  lty = c(1, 2)
)

```

Log Returns Normally Distributed?

Closer alligned to red line closer fit to normal distribution

```{r normality-check}
qqnorm(
  log_returns,
  main = paste(Chosen_Stock, ": Normal Q-Q Plot"))


qqline(log_returns, col = "red")
```

Check for Volatility Clustering

If consistently low or high then clustering

```{r volatility-clustering}
acf(
  log_returns^2,
  main = paste(Chosen_Stock, ": Autocorrelation of Squared Returns"))

```

Autoregressive Conditional Hetero Skedasticity test used to determine if a time series exhibits volatility cluttering. Smaller probability is high probability of an ARCH effect

```{r arch-test}
library(FinTS)
ArchTest(log_returns, lags = 10)

```

## Different Time Periods

```{r comparison-settings}
# Select stock
prices <- data_list[[Chosen_Stock]]$close
prices <- prices[is.finite(prices) & prices > 0]

# Historical estimation windows, measured in trading days
windows <- c(
  "1 month" = 21,
  "3 months" = 63,
  "6 months" = 126,
  "1 year" = 252,
  "2 years" = 504
)

# Forecast horizon: approximately one month
forecast_days <- 21
trading_days <- 252
```

For Different Periods

```{r}
compare_window <- function(prices, window, forecast_days = 21,
                           trading_days = 252) {
  
  # Error Handling
  if (length(prices) < window + forecast_days) {
    return(data.frame(
      Mean_APE = NA_real_,
      Median_APE = NA_real_,
      Mean_Annual_Volatility = NA_real_,
      Forecasts = 0
    ))
  }
  
  errors <- numeric(0)
  volatility_estimates <- numeric(0)
  
  # Rolling forecasts
  starts <- seq(
    from = window + 1,
    to = length(prices) - forecast_days + 1,
    by = forecast_days
  )
  
  for (i in starts) {
    
    estimation_prices <- prices[(i - window):(i - 1)]
    returns <- diff(log(estimation_prices))
    
    sigma_hat <- sd(returns) * sqrt(trading_days)
    mu_hat <- mean(returns) * trading_days +
      0.5 * sigma_hat^2
    
    S0 <- prices[i - 1]
    
    # Expected price after the forecast period
    predicted_price <- S0 * exp(
      mu_hat * forecast_days / trading_days
    )
    
    actual_price <- prices[i + forecast_days - 1]
    
    error <- abs(predicted_price - actual_price) /
      actual_price * 100
    
    errors <- c(errors, error)
    volatility_estimates <- c(volatility_estimates, sigma_hat)
  }
  
  data.frame(
    Mean_APE = mean(errors),
    Median_APE = median(errors),
    Mean_Annual_Volatility = mean(volatility_estimates),
    Forecasts = length(errors)
  )
}

# Compare each estimation window
comparison_list <- lapply(windows, function(w) {
  compare_window(prices, w, forecast_days, trading_days)
})

comparison <- do.call(rbind, comparison_list)
comparison$Period <- names(windows)
rownames(comparison) <- NULL

comparison <- comparison[, c(
  "Period", "Mean_APE", "Median_APE",
  "Mean_Annual_Volatility", "Forecasts"
)]

knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 3)
```
